description: MFA/2FA bypass techniques — step skip, code reuse, brute force, response manipulation

step_skip.description: Skip the MFA verification step by navigating directly to the post-MFA endpoint

probes.description: After successful password auth, skip the MFA challenge and request the post-auth page directly. If the session grants access without MFA completion, the step is skippable.

code_reuse.description: Reuse a previously valid MFA code after it should have expired

probes.description: Submit a previously used MFA code. If accepted, codes are not single-use.

brute_force.description: Brute-force short MFA codes (4-6 digits) without rate limiting

probes.description: Send multiple wrong codes rapidly. Check if the account locks or if rate limiting exists. A 4-digit code has 10K combinations; without lockout it is brute-forceable.

response_manipulation.description: Change the MFA verification response from failure to success

probes.description: Submit a wrong code and observe the failure response. If the client-side checks a boolean (success:true/false), intercepting and flipping it may bypass MFA.

null_value.description: Send null, empty, or zero-length MFA codes

probes.description: Submit empty MFA code. Some implementations skip validation on null/empty input.

backup_code_abuse.description: Use backup/recovery codes instead of TOTP to bypass MFA

probes.description: Check if backup codes are accepted on the MFA challenge endpoint. If the endpoint doesn't distinguish TOTP from backup codes, leaked backup codes bypass MFA permanently.

aitm_session_theft.description: Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) MFA bypass. The attacker proxies the login page (via evilginx2, Modlishka, or a reverse proxy). Victim authenticates normally through the proxy, completing MFA. The proxy captures the session cookie/token after MFA completes. No MFA replay needed — the attacker already has the post-MFA session. Only phishing-resistant auth (FIDO2/WebAuthn) prevents this.

probes.description: Detection: check if session tokens are bound to TLS channel (token binding / DPoP) — if not, AiTM can steal them

mfa_prompt_bombing.description: MFA prompt bombing (push notification fatigue). Attacker has valid credentials and sends repeated MFA push notifications until the victim approves one by mistake. Works against: Microsoft Authenticator (without number matching), Duo Push, Okta Push. Mitigated by number matching, FIDO2, or rate-limiting push requests.

probes.description: Check if the MFA push endpoint has rate limiting — send 5+ auth requests in rapid succession
